To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concentrations and composition of organic aerosols in Raipur are influenced by local emissions from coal burning, biomass burning, and plastics, with the latter being a new and potentially important source of organic aerosols.

(i) The organic compounds in the PM are mainly from fossil fuel utilization and burning of biomass and plastic, (ii) the concentrations of organic compounds are higher during winter, (iii) the concentrations of the organic compounds are higher in winter and lower in the summer.

organic aerosol particles in Raipur have a complex mixture of sources, with a significant influence from fossil fuel utilization and fugitive sources, and that new tracer compounds are present in the atmosphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of the chemical composition of organic aerosols in an extensively industrialized and coal mega-burning area of India, which is a major global emitter of particulate matter.
the characterization of organic compounds in PM, which is an essential step for the understanding and modeling of the atmospheric processes of organic aerosols and their effects on human health.
a better understanding of the sources and chemical composition of aerosol particles in a coal-burning region of central India.

the organic aerosol composition in the Raipur atmosphere is a mixture of primary and secondary sources of organic aerosols.
the organic aerosol particles are dominated by fossil-fuel combustion, with the presence of a large number of new organic tracer compounds that have not been identified before in aerosol samples.
the organic aerosol composition of the Raipur area is a mixture of anthropogenic and natural sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organic aerosols in the ambient air of the industrial area of Raipur are mainly composed of fossil fuel combustion, biomass burning, and fugitive emissions.
organic tracers of aerosol particles in Raipur are mainly from fossil fuel combustion and fugitive emissions.

the organic composition of aerosol particles in Raipur is dominated by fossil-fuel combustion emissions, with a significant contribution of biomass burning, and fugitive emissions from industrial activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the organic aerosols of Raipur are mainly derived from anthropogenic sources, and the organic composition is strongly influenced by local sources and meteorological conditions.

the chemical composition and source of organic compounds of ambient PM in the industrialized area of Chhattisgarhi are different from those reported in the literature for other parts of India, and the organic compounds in the ambient air of this region are dominated by emissions from fossil fuel usage and burning of plastics.

the composition of the organic compounds in aerosol particles in Raipur is complex, with a large contribution from anthropogenic sources, and the presence of a large number of potential new tracers that can be useful in source apportionment.
